The New East Side Fire Department of Chicago is recruiting new firefighters for the weekend shifts. The weekend starts at Friday 4:00 PM and ends at Monday 7:00 AM.
During this period of time, there are 3 shifts every day:
From 7:00 AM to 3:00 PM
From 3:00 PM to 11:00 PM
From 10:00 PM to 8:00 AM
The standard procedure in the department states that there must be at least 3 teams in each shift. Each team must have at least 10 firefighters.
The department manager declared that each firefighter can work only one shift a day, and after completing his shift he must rest for at least the duration of the next two shifts before taking another shift.

What is the minimal number of firefighters required to work during the weekend, taking into consideration that each firefighter must rest at least two shifts before taking another shift?
questions.explanation:
The right answer is C

There are 3 different shifts every day and we are asked to calculate the minimum number of firefighters required to fulfill the requirement of no more than 1 shift per day for every firefighter who work during the weekend (rest is defined as 2 shifts).
Although the minimum amount of teams in each shift is 3, and at least 10 firefighters are in each team (3*3*10 =90), 90 is not the correct answer.

Firefighters are at a fire incident at a four-story residential building. Luckily all victims were safely rescued from the building. While several firefighters execute procedures for property conservation, another department member talks to witnesses to try and determine possible clues for the cause of fire. The witnesses gave the following accounts:

Witness 1: "I live on the 4th floor. Since this morning my apartment was having electricity failures. At 10 o'clock I noticed someone screaming 'Fire, Fire' so I took a look on the corridor and there was smoke coming from the staircase which is very close to my apartment door. I grabbed some of my belongings and walked to the other side of the corridor to the emergency staircase and went down to the garden. I'm happy the fire didn't reach my floor and I have somewhere to sleep tonight."

Witness 2: "I heard screams outside my apartment door this morning. I opened the door and saw some firefighters evacuating people from their houses. I was a bit surprised as there wasn't any apparent smoke or fire. I got out of the building from the entrance lobby and saw many of my neighbors outside. They told me someone was rescued by the fire crews but he had a smoke inhalation injury."

Witness 3: "This morning I went outside of my house and smelled a strong smell of something burning. It came from the staircase so I went to check it out and I saw smoke coming out of the power box. I knew it was very dangerous so I called 911 and simultaneously I tried to warn as many neighbors as I could. I saw Mark and Judy in the hallway so I told them to warn the people upstairs. Then, suddenly there was an explosion, and the power box caught on fire. The next thing I remember is waking up at the ambulance with paramedics around me."

Witness 4: "Gary, my neighbor told me there was a fire in the building and asked me and my sister Judy to worn the other residents. My sister ran up one floor to warn people, while I ran up one floor above it which is the highest one. Later, I wanted to go back to my sister but the fire spread and I couldn't use the staircase. It was all dark because the electricity shut down but I managed to reach the end of the corridor and escape. Downstairs I saw my sister safe and sound. Later I heard the sad news that Gary was injured by the smoke."

According to the witness accounts, the fire started at the ___ floor and spread to the ___ floor.
questions.explanation:
The right answer is D.

According to the accounts of witness 4, he went up 2 floors to the last one which is the 4th. That means he started at the 2nd floor. Witness 4 met witness 3 in the hallway of the 2nd floor, and by the account of witness 3 the fire started there and he couldn't go down to the 3rd later because of the spreading fire. From the account of witness 1 we know that the fire hadn't reached the 4th floor so we can understand it only reached the 3rd floor.

He didn't stop quickly enough and back ended a green Acura, which in turn, hit the motorcyclist in front of it. At first the driver tried to increase his speed to make the light, but then realized he would not make it and slammed on the brakes. Which witnesses report is most likely to be correct?

In May 2015, the New York Fire Department received a call to respond to a reported accident involving a private car and a tanker truck. It was taken into consideration that hazardous materials may be involved or specialized equipment may be needed. The accident took place on Route 30, south of the intersection of Main Street and north of the intersection of Park Avenue. The tanker was an 8,000-gallon-capacity aluminum MC-306, loaded with 7,200 gallons of gasoline. A black SUV, which headed north, made a dangerous overtaking and collided "head-on" with the tanker. The tanker overturned, opened up, and began losing its fuel. The SUV crashed on the concrete median strip.

As the companies approached the scene, radio transmissions from first-due units confirmed that a black SUV, was 100 ft. away from the truck and was fully consumed in a fire. 4 passengers were trapped in the fire, and their life was in danger. The truck's driver managed to escape from the tractor.

After the initial size-up of the scene, team Alpha from company 288 placed their apparatus 30 ft. from the SUV. The team took control on the fire, assessed the medical condition of the passengers, stabilized the car and used their tools to disassemble the car door. Simultaneously, the firefighters of team Bravo from the same company placed their apparatus 40 ft. from the tanker and scanned for any uncontrolled fire around it. The team also applied Fluoroprotein foam concentrate into the sewage system to prevent the gasoline that entered the system from exploding. The SUV was fully extricated and all the passengers were taken to the nearby hospital with an ambulance.

20 minutes later, gasoline from the tanker reached the SUV, and a small flame ignited. All the gasoline that filled the street caught fire and an explosion occurred in the tanker. At that moment, the incident commander ordered teams Alpha and Bravo to evacuate the entire road within a radius of 800 meters and to take into consideration the north wind. The teams evacuated the area from all civilians and emergency teams against the wind direction. All engine companies moved their apparatus 300 ft. or more away. The commander decided to not extinguish the fire, but rather let the truck continue to burn until the fire was suppressed and the situation was stabilized.

Although it could have ended much worse, the incident ended with one death – a man that died from inhaling the thick smoke from the explosion. The teams were highly praised for the quick evacuation and the professional extrication that saved the lives of many. In contrast, the incident commander was criticized for his late decision to evacuate the area, but the decision to let the fire burn-out put his function in a positive light.

What were the initial missions of teams Alpha and Bravo?
choices: Team Alpha was responsible for extrication and rescue and team Bravo for identification and prevention of hazards.
Team Alpha and Bravo were both responsible for fire stabilization.
Team Alpha was responsible for car extrication and team Bravo for evacuation.
Team Alpha was responsible for evacuation of the area and team Bravo for identification and prevention of hazards.
questions.explanation:
The right answer is A.

From the actions of team Alpha and Bravo we can understand their missions.

Team Alpha actions:
-Placed the apparatus close to the SUV
-Controlled the fire on the SUV
-Checked the victims inside
-Removed the car door

The list of actions implies that their mission was to extricate (and rescue) the passengers from the SUV.

Team Bravo actions:
-Scanned for any uncontrolled fire (this is a hazard)
-Applied Fluoroprotein foam concentrate into the sewage system to prevent explosion

Their actions imply that their mission was identification and prevention of hazards such as gasoline spill or fire.

We can eliminate answers C and D because evacuation cannot be considered initial mission, as the teams evacuated the area after the incident escalated.
